key_insight: The paper shows that one-step image editing can be made more reliable by choosing the best update size after the initial transport step, instead of using a fixed strength for all edits. This balances prompt adherence and source-image preservation without adding a slower iterative editor.
problem_solved: One-step diffusion editors face a trade-off: the update must be strong enough to achieve the requested edit, but weak enough to keep the original image intact. A single fixed step size cannot handle different edit types well.
method: Treats editing as a post-hoc candidate-selection problem rather than training a new editing model.
Uses Riemannian Residual Line Search to search over candidate transport updates and select the residual that best matches the edit objective.
Balances two competing goals during selection: semantic change toward the target prompt and fidelity to the source image.
impact: This makes one-step editors more practical by improving quality without sacrificing speed. For practitioners, it offers a lightweight way to improve edit reliability across diverse prompts and image types.
visual_elements: A balance-scale diagram showing 'edit strength' vs 'image preservation'.

paper_title: Bridging the Manifold Gap: Riemannian Residual Line Search for One-Step Image Editing
paper_authors: Hongzhu Yi, Zhongtian Luo, Tong Li, Yiyan Fan, Jungang Xu
